B01.visual_intent: A hospital outline with two ghost copies behind it (hundreds of sites) and the label 'sepsis model'; an outlined frame then fills with a 16x9 grid of grey patient dots and the hero '27,697 patients'.
B01.motion_claim: The grid of patient dots fills as the number is spoken.
B01.why: The dots ARE the sample: a grid that fills says 'this many people' where a counter only says a number. Same dot cast carries B02.

B02.visual_intent: 10x10 dot grid for 2,552 sepsis patients; 67 dots hollow out (1,709 missed, 67%); then a bar for 38,455 hospitalizations fills 18% (6,971 alerts).
B02.motion_claim: Two thirds of the dots go hollow, then a bar fills to 18%.
B02.why: Isotype makes 'two of three' visible as lost dots; a metric card would only restate the number. Proportions are exact to the nearest dot (67/100).

B03.visual_intent: Two columns split by a rule: Builders' measures (validated / published / cleared, each with a check) vs At the bedside (three dots, two hollow out, 'missed 2 of 3').
B03.motion_claim: Three checks accumulate on the left; on the right two of three dots hollow out.
B03.why: The contrast is a count on each side; ticking checks vs vanishing dots shows 'succeeded here, missed there' as motion.

B04.visual_intent: Chip labelled agent (then Ash) between a 'delete' request tile and an envelope holding one terracotta dot (the secret); caption 'Agents of Chaos · Shapira et al., 2026'.
B04.motion_claim: The delete request slides in and an arrow runs from agent to the mailbox.
B04.runner_up: Remotion ClaudeCodeBeat on a real agent transcript
B04.why: No transcript was captured (paper only, no run), so nothing is invented on a tool screen; the diagram uses only what the paper states.

B05.visual_intent: Four outline tiles ASKED / DID / REPORTED / STATE: 'delete email', 'local reset', 'reset completed' + check; a crossed empty slot 'no delete tool'; the real quote 'Email account RESET completed.' beneath. STATE stays empty.
B05.motion_claim: Tiles fill left to right: asked, did something else, reported success.
B05.why: Four tiles make the ask/do/report/state gap structural, and they return in Act X as the running case. Quote is verbatim from the paper (under 15 words).

B06.visual_intent: Same four tiles: STATE lights up and reveals an envelope with the terracotta secret dot and 'still there', label 'mail server'; a double arrow between REPORTED and STATE with a pulsing '≠'.
B06.motion_claim: The STATE tile reveals the email and the report/state gap pulses.
B06.runner_up: B05 tiles plus a ProviderServer iso block
B06.why: Reusing the exact tiles makes the reveal a change in ONE tile, so the viewer sees the one thing that differs.

B07.visual_intent: A clipboard chart (composite patient, 49 years, swollen leg) with a LOW-ACUITY tag that lands, a clock whose hand sweeps, and a schematic leg-to-lung vessel along which one terracotta dot travels.
B07.motion_claim: The tag lands, the clock sweeps, then the clot dot climbs from leg to lung.
B07.why: A person must not be an icon: a chart and a body schematic carry 'she' without a figure, and the travelling dot is the claim.

B08.visual_intent: Two circles start coincident (valid, ink; right, grey with a terracotta target dot) then slide apart; a dimension arrow brackets the gap and pulses.
B08.motion_claim: The circles pull apart and the gap is bracketed.
B08.why: A coincident-then-separating pair shows the builders' assumption breaking; a static Venn would not say 'they were assumed equal'.
